key_insight: The paper asks whether DiffusionGemma is harder to understand because more of its computation happens in a continuous latent space. It frames transparency as two parts—being able to interpret intermediate states and being able to infer the algorithm the model is implementing—and uses that lens to assess how transparent the model really is.
problem_solved: It addresses the challenge of interpreting reasoning in diffusion-based language models, where hidden computation is distributed across continuous intermediate snapshots rather than discrete token steps. This makes it harder to inspect what the model is doing, why it makes a decision, and whether it is behaving in a predictable or debuggable way.
method: Decompose transparency into two dimensions: variable transparency (can we interpret intermediate states?) and algorithmic transparency (can we recover the underlying computation?).
Analyze DiffusionGemma’s latent-space computation through intermediate snapshots to see how much reasoning signal is observable at different stages.
Compare the transparency of diffusion-style computation against the more familiar token-based reasoning paradigm.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this helps clarify when diffusion-based models are inspectable, debuggable, and safer to deploy. It provides a framework for evaluating transparency beyond standard token-level explanations, which is especially relevant for models with continuous internal representations.
visual_elements: A split diagram showing the two transparency dimensions: variable vs. algorithmic.
A timeline or diffusion-step ladder illustrating intermediate latent snapshots.
A side-by-side comparison of token-based reasoning vs. continuous latent reasoning.
An icon-based framework map showing interpretability, debugging, safety, and misuse mitigation.
paper_authors: Joshua Engels, Callum McDougall, Bilal Chughtai, Janos Kramar, Senthoran Rajamanoharan
